source_statement: Let Γ be a circle, and ω1 and ω2 be two non-intersecting circles inside Γ that are internally tangent to Γ at X1 and X2 , respectively. Let one of the common internal tangents of ω1 and ω2 touch ω1 and ω2 at T1 and T2 , respectively, while intersecting Γ at two points A and B. Given that 2X1 T1 = X2 T2 and that ω1 , ω2 , and Γ have radii 2, 3, and 12, respectively, compute the length of AB.

clause_ledger.source: Gamma radius12; omega1/omega2 radii2,3 internally tangent at X1,X2
clause_ledger.dsl: use the common internal tangent as y=0, O=(0,h), O1=(sqrt(100-(h-2)^2),2), O2=(sqrt(81-(h+3)^2),-3), and construct X1,X2 on Gamma along the center radii; the original internal-tangency constraints are retained

clause_ledger.source: common internal tangent touches at T1,T2 and meets Gamma at A,B
clause_ledger.dsl: L is the x-axis, T1,T2 are the tangent feet, and A,B are its Gamma intersections
